item.title: [NBC Sports] Vinnie Pasquantino hits grand slam in loss Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Nick Shlain; Vinnie Pasquantino
item.description:
Vinnie Pasquantino went 3-for-5 with three runs scored, a double, a grand slam and five RBI against the White Sox on Tuesday.
Pasquantino’s home run was his 15th of the season. He hit a grand slam off Luis Castillo in the ninth inning. Pasquantino has had a down season, but suddenly has six home runs and 18 RBI in 18 games in September. He’s hitting .259 with a .751 OPS and 59 RBI with five games left in the regular season.

item.content:encoded:
The last time I was physically here at Kauffman Stadium for a baseball game was on September 4, where I witnessed Daniel Lynch IV immediately give up five runs in two innings and functionally take the Royals out of the contest before it began. I got worked up enough about it that I wrote about it that weekend, where I said that the Lynch starter experiment was going exactly how everyone knew it would because of Lynch’s inability to get right-handed batters out with his awful changeup. I linked multiple videos of Lynch hanging changes on a line to those righties.
You can therefore imagine my displeasure at walking into the clubhouse this afternoon, checking my phone to see who was officially starting, and seeing Lynch’s name pop up. I feared a Groundhog’s Day situation.
Unfortunately for me and the meager collection of Royals die-hards watching in person, that’s what happened. The White Sox crushed Royals pitching to the tune of 14 runs, and no amount of late game heroics could lessen the gap. Final score: 14-11, White Sox.
It began early. Witness this rocket line drive off a changeup in the first inning! It was from right-handed batter Chase Meidroth.
Oh, and this laser of an opposite-field home run from right-handed Brenton Doyle. It came off, you guessed it, a changeup.
And this—hark! Another Meidroth homer off another changeup!
After three innings, the White Sox had thwomped their way to a 6-0 lead, which was cut to a whole 6-1 lead by a solo Nick Loftin home run in the bottom of the sixth.
But Lynch was still pitching, and so you could probably bet that five-run lead might balloon further. Sure enough, it did. In the fourth inning, Lynch managed to get two outs but then ran into a row of right-handed batters and, well. You know what happened. Miguel Vargas single, Tommy Pham walk, Randal Grichuk home run. 9-1, White Sox.
At this point, I packed up my belongings and left to listen to the game on the drive and follow from home. Getting credentials is an honor, but what is also great is that, since I’m not a beat writer, I can bail when it’s clear that postgame pressers are not going to yield any particularly interesting pieces of information. Both teams packed it in after the seventh inning; the White Sox removed Miguel Vargas, Tommy Pham, and Braden Montgomery, while the Royals removed Bobby Witt Jr. and Salvador Perez.
Kansas City’s offense, however, did not go quietly into the night. The Royals struck in three consecutive innings against Chicago starter Anthony Kay, with Witt accruing three hits. They managed a trio of runs against Trevor Richards in the eighth, with a pair of extra base hits by the Italian Stallions Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino providing the power. And then, in the ninth inning, Tyler Tolbert singled, and Caglianone singled, and Maikel Garcia worked his third walk of the game. Pasquantino then crushed a grand slam to right-center field. It was glorious.
But any hope the Royals had of a great comeback was stymied by, you guessed it, the bullpen. In his Royals debut and his 2026 debut, Tony Gonsolin—who has only pitched 36 MLB innings the last two seasons due to injury—pitched two clean innings and exploded in the seventh, giving up a double to Grichuk and a homer to Munetaka Murakami. Then, he loaded the bases and walked home another run, which prompted Matt Quatraro to remove him in favor of Nolan Hoffman. Hoffman immediately gave up a single to Andrew Benintendi to push the score to 14-4.
As a result, even though the Royals scored 11 runs, they didn’t score a single run down by less than six. Since August 30, the Royals have won two (2) games where they have scored fewer than five runs. That’s because they’ve given up, on average, 5.5 games during that 20-game span.
This is the Royals’ fifth consecutive loss, their eighth loss in their last nine games, and their 15th in their last 20. Remember when the Royals won 13 of 15? They were 13 games under .500 after that first win.
Tonight, the Royals officially wipe all those gains away, and are now 13 games under again. Winning 70 games seems like a longshot. Eat Arby’s.

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to “Stock Up, Stock Down,” where every week, the Royals On SI staff writers highlight Kansas City Royals players who have stood out or had a rough week. From the lineup to the pitching staff, we’ll dive into who is trending up and who is trending down.
Kansas City did not have its best week, going 1-5 over the last seven days. The Royals’ lone win came during their series loss to the Houston Astros. Let’s take a look at some players who stood out and some who sat down.
Stock Up: Players Who Stood Out Over the Past Week
Daniel Lynch IV
In the Royals’ lone win over the past week, Daniel Lynch IV had his best start of the season since joining the rotation. Lynch tossed five strong innings, allowing just two hits, no earned runs and striking out three.
Lynch was having a fantastic year out of the bullpen, serving as a bright spot for a group that has struggled all season. Kansas City decided to test Lynch in the rotation, but unfortunately, his production has not been the same as it was in the bullpen. This week, however, he was able to get things rolling.
Vinnie Pasquantino
Vinnie Pasquantino has swung the bat very well over the last week, putting on a power display. Over the last seven days, he is slashing .375/.412/.938, with three of his hits being home runs.
This is an encouraging sign from the first baseman, who has had a limited season due to injuries and a slow start to the year. Pasquantino is looking to finish the season on a strong note.
Nick Loftin
Utility man Nick Loftin has had a hot stretch at the plate over the past week. He has posted a .438 average in his last 16 at-bats. His plate approach has looked great, as he has struck out just once and recorded a double as well.
Stock Down: Players Who Struggled Over the Past Week
Nate Pearson
Relief arm Nate Pearson did not have his best stuff over the past seven days. In just 2 2/3 innings, he allowed six earned runs on seven hits, including one home run. He struck out three as the right-hander looks to bounce back and finish the year strong.
Maikel Garcia
Maikel Garcia has not been at his best since returning from the injured list. In his first 16 at-bats back in the lineup, the third baseman has recorded just one hit. He has collected two RBIs but appears to be dealing with a slow start since returning from the injury.
Kyle Isbel
Much like Garcia, Kyle Isbel has not been seeing the ball well at the plate. He has collected just one hit in his last 13 at-bats and has struck out four times. The hope is the center fielder can finish the year strong following this slump.

item.content:encoded:
A rainy afternoon in Pittsburgh sent the first baseman to the cages early, and the work showed up in the biggest swing of the day.
They did, and he delivered a two-run homer in the seventh inning that put Kansas City ahead.
The lead did not survive an eighth-inning homer by Pittsburgh, and the Royals lost the road finale 4-3, but the way Pasquantino handled an unusual assignment was the most interesting part of a long afternoon.
Built and Lost
Kansas City scored first when first baseman Salvador Perez singled home shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. in the opening inning.
Center fielder Oneil Cruz tied it with a solo homer in the fourth, and first baseman Spencer Horwitz singled home the go-ahead run off starter Michael Wacha in the sixth.
In the seventh, left fielder John Rave reached on a bunt single and moved up on a groundout, and Pasquantino, hitting for center fielder Tyler Tolbert, drove a two-run homer to right center off reliever Carmen Mlodzinski for a 3-2 lead.
Catcher Rafael Flores Jr. answered with a two-run homer in the eighth, and a ninth-inning double by catcher Luke Maile went to waste when the tying run was stranded at third base.
Ready Before He Was Needed
His explanation afterward said plenty about how he goes about the job.
"I got prepared early because I wasn't sure if we would play a full nine innings because of the rain. So I came inside (to the indoor batting) cages in the third or fourth inning. You never feel totally prepared when you come in and pinch-hit in the middle of the game, but I felt good."
Preparation like that usually comes from habit.
Pinch-hitting asks a player to deliver one good at-bat with no rhythm behind it, which makes the preparation part of the job, and Pasquantino treated it that way in a game with nothing on the line.
Wacha did his part too, throwing 113 pitches to protect a tired bullpen because he sensed the relievers needed the rest.
Home for the Final Six
The road schedule is finished, and it ends with Kansas City at 28-53 away from home after a 2-7 trip.
The season closes with six games at Kauffman Stadium, three against the White Sox starting Tuesday and three against the Guardians over the weekend, two clubs separated by one game in the AL Central race.
If the rest of the roster prepares the way Pasquantino did on Sunday, the White Sox and Guardians will have to earn every win they get in Kansas City.

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Cristopher Sánchez earned his major league-leading 18th win Sunday, leading the Philadelphia Phillies to a 7-2 victory over the New York Mets.
The Phillies (86-70), who salvaged a split of the four-game series, entered Sunday in the third National League wild-card spot, one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four games clear of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Sánchez surrendered six hits — including Bo Bichette’s sixth-inning homer — and struck out six over 6 1/3 innings as he snapped a tie with the Boston Red Sox’s Sonny Gray for the big league lead in wins.

The last Phillies pitcher to lead the majors in wins was Steve Carlton with 23 in 1982.
Justin Crawford had a three-run triple and Luis Arraez finished with two RBIs. Alec Bohm and Trea Turner each had run-scoring hits. Kyle Schwarber tied a career high with four walks.
Rookie Jonah Tong (2-2) gave up four runs and struck out five in 4 2/3 innings for the last-place Mets, who finished 36-45 at home — their worst record at Citi Field since the 2013 team went 33-48.
PIRATES 4, ROYALS 3
PITTSBURGH (AP) — Rafael Flores Jr. hit the go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to help Pittsburgh to a win over Kansas City and complete a series sweep.
After Ryan O’Hearn led off with a single to center, Flores sent a slider from Nate Pearson (2-3) into the left-field bleachers for his 10th homer this season.
Pittsburgh rallied with a two-run homer in the eighth for a second straight day. Brandon Lowe had his 33rd of the season in a 6-5 win Saturday.
Carmen Mlodzinki (8-7) got the win. He allowed two runs and three hits in three innings. The reliever gave up a pinch-hit, two-run home run to Vinnie Pasquantino that gave Kansas City a 3-2 lead with two outs in the seventh.
Mason Montgomery earned his 16th save. He retired the first two batters in the ninth before Luke Maile hit a double and took third on a fielding error by Jake Mangum. Montgomery got Isaac Collins to fly out to right to strand Maile.
The Royals went ahead 1-0 in the first inning with three straight singles off Lake Bachar. Bobby Witt Jr. beat out a groundball to second baseman Lowe. He moved to third on a single to right from Jac Caglianone and scored when Perez shot one through the middle of the infield.
RAYS 5, RED SOX 1
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Griffin Jax tossed five shutout innings and the Tampa Bay crept closer to the AL East title with a victory over Boston.
The Rays will have an opportunity to clinch the franchise’s fifth division title during Tuesday’s doubleheader at the New York Yankees.
Boston would have clinched a playoff spot with a victory. The Red Sox, who were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East on June 24, have since gone 52-25. They could still wrap up a spot Sunday with a Houston loss.
Jax (8-10) allowed three singles and worked out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth inning by striking out Roman Anthony. Cole Sulser, Brody Hopkins and Steven Matz each pitched an inning of scoreless relief.
Boston’s Trevor Story spoiled the shutout in the ninth with a one-out home run off right-hander Ty Johnson.
The Rays scored four first-inning runs off left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-7). Jonny DeLuca smashed a two-run, bases-loaded double down the left-field line and Chandler Simpson followed with a two-run single. Sandoval began the inning by walking Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade, then surrendering a single to Junior Caminero.
CUBS 9, REDS 1
CINCINNATI (AP) — Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run as Chicago moved closer to clinching a postseason berth with a victory over Cincinnati.
Chicago (87-69) reduced its magic number to one and could wrap up a berth if the Diamondbacks lose to the Yankees later Sunday.
The Cubs began the day tied with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot which would earn them home-field advantage in the wild-card round. The Cubs own the tiebreakers over the Diamondbacks, Padres, and Phillies.
Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday’s game in the fourth inning after being struck in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while standing near the on-deck circle.
Cubs left-hander David Peterson (9-8) allowed a run on three hits in seven innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.
The Cubs loaded the bases with one out in the third. Ian Happ singled in a run and Nico Hoerner walked to force in another to extend Chicago’s lead to 3-0. Pedro Ramirez’s two-run single made the score 5-0.
Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12) allowed five earned runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts.
CARDINALS 5, NATIONALS 3
ST. LOUIS (AP) — Iván Herrera hit a pair of home runs, and Leo Bernal also homered as St. Louis scored three runs in the eighth inning to come from behind and beat Washington.
Bernal hit his fifth homer of the season off Yovanny Cruz (0-2) after Erik Tolman walked Jordan Walker with two outs in the eighth inning.
Herrera hit his second homer of the game and 18th of the season to tie the game at 3-all after hitting a solo shot in the first inning.
It was Herrera’s third career multi-homer game and second this season after going deep twice on June 13 at Minnesota.
Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless eighth inning for St. Louis, and Riley O’Brien pitched a perfect ninth to earn his National League-leading 38th save.
Cardinals starter Quinn Mathews allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks in a career-high seven innings.
Jake Irvin allowed two runs on three hits and had eight strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings for the Nationals.

item.title: [MLB.com] Garcia's clutch hit vs. reigning Cy Young winner a bright spot in tough 2026
item.dc:creator: John Perrotto
item.description: Garcia is thankful to be back in the starting lineup for the final days of the 2026 regular season. He has been limited to just 76 games, because of a partial tear of his left hamstring and just returned from the injured list on Tuesday after missing 21 games. “I didn’t think I might play again this year, so I’m thankful,” Garcia said following Friday night’s 8-5 loss to the Pirates to open a three-game series at PNC Park. “I just wish there were more games left.” Garcia had high hopes for 2026
item.content:encoded:
Garcia is thankful to be back in the starting lineup for the final days of the 2026 regular season. He has been limited to just 76 games, because of a partial tear of his left hamstring and just returned from the injured list on Tuesday after missing 21 games.
“I didn’t think I might play again this year, so I’m thankful,” Garcia said following Friday night’s 8-5 loss to the Pirates to open a three-game series at PNC Park. “I just wish there were more games left.”
Garcia had high hopes for 2026 after making his first All-Star Game appearance last season, then signing a five-year, $57.5 million contract extension that runs through 2030 and includes a club option for ‘31.
Alas, Garcia is slashing .262/.318/.378 with three home runs.
However, the 26-year-old provided a bright spot against Pittsburgh in what turned out to be a frustrating night for Kansas City. Garcia’s two-run double in the third inning helped the Royals build a 4-0 lead against reigning National League Cy Young winner Paul Skenes.
Still, they eventually lost for the 12th time in their last 17 games despite home runs by Vinnie Pasquantino and Michael Massey.
“We think the world of Mikey,” manager Matt Quatraro said of Garcia. “We committed a lot of years and a lot of money to him, because we think he’s a really good player who can help us win. Getting him back on the field is important for us, and it’s good for him, too.
“He probably thought his season was over, but he worked very hard through the rehab process to get back. And he got a big hit in a big spot.”
Just eight games remain for the Royals, so there isn’t a whole lot of season left to salvage for Garcia. Yet, he appreciates what few days remain and getting a big hit off a Cy Young winner.
“I like to face the best pitchers,” Garcia said with a smile. “It makes me fight that much harder. It felt really good to get a big hit there with a couple of guys on base. It’s been a tough year for me personally, but we have come back here, we want to finish the season healthy, and we want to help the team win some games. I want to go home for the winter with a good feeling.”
The usually unflappable Randy Dobnak admittedly was fighting some feelings when he took the mound in his hometown for just the second time in his career. The right-hander grew up in suburban South Park, Pa.
Dobnak’s previous appearance at PNC Park came with the Twins in 2020. However, fans weren’t permitted to attend games during that pandemic-shortened season. Dobnak estimated he had at least 200 family members and friends in the stands and had attended approximately 300 games in this ballpark.
“This was really kind of special,” Dobnak said. “After I threw my last warm-up pitch, I stood there on the mound and took it all in. Growing up, this was the place I always wanted to be. I caught myself almost getting a little bit emotional out there.”
Dobnak paused and chuckled.
“That quickly changed when I threw my first pitch and [Konnor] Griffin singled right back up the middle,” he said.
Unfortunately for Dobnak and his throng of supporters, that signaled what was to come. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on seven hits and two walks, while striking out one.
Dobnak left with a 5-3 lead, but the Pirates rallied against the Royals’ bullpen. Spencer Horwitz’s two-run single off Nate Pearson in a three-run seventh inning broke a 5-5 tie.
“I think the biggest thing was first-pitch strikes with Randy,” Quatraro said. “It was an interesting game for him. There were four hits down the third-base line from a left-handed hitter and a couple of infield hits. He had a lot of traffic to deal with.”
